column11: 0.5 x the fitted PCSK9 anchor, against lly_solbinsiran.csv's 0.25, and the difference IS the judgement. The anchor is the same: the PCSK9 inhibitors, the last high-priced injectable lipid class to launch into a prevalent US pool against payer prior authorisation. In Cardiology Consultants of Philadelphia, 97 cardiologists (Smith A et al., J Clin Med 2021;10:3828, doi 10.3390/jcm10173828, PMC8432238, Table 2), the yearly share of eligible ASCVD patients newly prescribed one was 0.26% in 2015 (from the July launch), 1.23% in 2016, 1.09% in 2017, 1.52% in 2018 and 1.60% in 2019, which a logistic of peak 0.0142, k 3.06 and midpoint -0.55 fits to an rmse of 0.17 points. 0.5 x 0.0142 = 0.0071. WHY DOUBLE SOLBINSIRAN'S MULTIPLE: the solbinsiran seed sets 0.25 on the explicit ground that solbinsiran 'would be the third RNA drug into sHTG after olezarsen (approved June 2026) and plozasiran, both APOC3, which cut triglycerides by about 80% in sHTG (SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 medians of 79% and 81%, Arrowhead 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-06-30) against solbinsiran's 58% to 60% in mixed dyslipidaemia'. Plozasiran IS the drug that seed names as arriving ahead of it with the better effect, and it is second rather than third
column12: Arrowhead's own 10-K confirms the readout the multiple leans on: 'Arrowhead presented results from the pivotal Phase 3 SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 studies of plozasiran in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG)' and 'SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 met their primary and all prespecified secondary endpoints and demonstrated deep and durable reductions in TGs, with median reductions from baseline of 79% and 81%, respectively, at Month 12 (p<0.0001 in both studies)' (ARWR FY2026 10-K, arwr-20260930.htm). Against the multiple: olezarsen was approved in sHTG in June 2026 and is quarterly-dosed too, so plozasiran enters second, not first; and every sHTG entrant faces the same prior-authorisation wall the PCSK9 series measures

The label covers FCS and nothing else: 'REDEMPLO is indicated as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS)' (DailyMed setid 7fd37993-f85a-4af1-8bbe-133299f226ed, SPL version 4, effective 2026-08-31, the Redemplo row in the book's labels table), confirmed by the filer: 'The FDA approved REDEMPLO (plozasiran) as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides (TGs) in adults with Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome ("FCS")' (ARWR FY2026 10-K). FCS patients have triglycerides far above 500 mg/dL, so they sit INSIDE the sHTG pool above and are already sold to. Size: 'FCS is an autosomal recessive disorder that affects approximately 1 to 10 individuals per million' (Aguilar-Salinas CA et al., 'A multi-society Delphi consensus statement on the diagnosis of familial chylomicronemia syndrome', Arch Endocrinol Metab 2025;69(5):e250071, doi 10.20945/2359-4292-2025-0071, PMID 41026863, PMC12483350). 10 per million, the top of the range, on the 340,110,988 US residents at 1 July 2024 (Census Vintage 2024) = 3,401, over the 711,850 eligible patients the rows above give: 0.004778
column12: THE RANGE IS TENFOLD AND THE TOP OF IT IS TAKEN ON PURPOSE: at 1 per million the overlap would be 0.000478 and the expansion worth 0.43% more. Choosing the top means this row cannot flatter the readout. Neither end changes the valuation materially, which is itself the finding - FCS is a rounding error against severe hypertriglyceridemia, and essentially all of Redemplo's value sits in the sHTG expansion this catalyst gates. One thing the overlap does NOT capture: NCT06822790 is 'A Phase 3 Open-Label Extension Study to Evaluate the Long-Term Safety and Efficacy of Plozasiran in Adults With Hypertriglyceridemia (SHASTA-10 Study)', 710 enrolled actual, rolling over participants from parent studies AROAPOC3-2003, -3001, -3003, -3004 and -3009 (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, read 2026-11-14). Those parents include the FCS programme as well as the sHTG ones, so some of the 710 are already-labelled patients; the layer values the sHTG population, not the trial roster
